parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment explicitly states an action: "It would be better to conduct a significance test on the experimental results." This is a direct suggestion, and the action is well-defined: authors know they should run a statistical significance test on their reported experimental results (the accuracy across 15 runs compared with the best baseline), which is a standard methodological step. The comment also motivates the action concretely by pointing to the overlapping standard deviations of the proposed method and the best baseline, so the scope of the analysis is clear. While the comment does not name a specific statistical test (e.g., t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test), the rubric's concreteness standard is whether authors know exactly what modification to make and how to apply it; 'conduct a significance test on the experimental results' tells authors precisely what analysis to run and on what data, so the absence of a named test does not make the action vague. Therefore, the comment contains both an explicit action and concrete details on how to implement it, matching the rubric's highest category.
